### What this release delivers

`sememe conform <tx.json> --store <dir>` resolves each instruction's accounts by index into the canonical key list (`keys[index]`). In v0.4.16 an index that did not resolve (past the end, negative, or a non-integer entry such as the `jsonParsed` object shape) became `{address: null, signer: null, writable: null}`, and `checkAccountList` files a null signer under `unknownSigner`: a note, never a violation.

**The worst face, measured on the order-engine fixture** (committed fixture, no network): the fill instruction carries the transaction's ONE real disagreement — a signing account the interface does not declare, at position 11. Replacing exactly that index with an out-of-range value:

```
intact transaction:          verdict undeclared-signing-account, EXIT 1
broken extra account index:  verdict remaining-accounts,        EXIT 0
whole transaction in jsonParsed object shape:      remaining-accounts, EXIT 0
```

The disagreement was not just unchecked — it was **hidden**, behind a green CI gate.

### Install

```bash
npm install github:auroraxo/sememe#v0.4.17   # tagged release; no npm account needed
```

### What changed

One refusal, `instruction-account-index-unresolvable`, raised **before** the store is read and **before** the filter selection:

- any instruction whose accounts list carries an index the key list cannot resolve is refused, naming each offending instruction (top-level `#n`, or `CPI of top-level #n at position p`), the account POSITION, and the RAW value it carried, plus the repair;
- CPI instructions are covered;
- `jsonParsed` object entries are refused by name instead of folding into null rows;
- guards: an unresolvable PROGRAM index keeps `instruction-program-id-unresolvable` even beside broken accounts, an EMPTY accounts list stays legal, and loaded-range (ALT) indices stay resolvable.

### Evidence

- `research/conform-unresolvable-accounts-2026-11-11.json` — same probe in the pre-fix tree (`git archive 7b30c68` = published v0.4.16) and this tree: pre-fix 3 of 4 defect shapes exit 0 and the disagreement is hidden (`hiddenDisagreement: true`); this tree refuses all 4 with the named reason; both controls unchanged in both trees.
- `research/conform-unresolvable-accounts-tag-2026-11-11.json` — installed tags in empty directories: v0.4.16 carries the defect (exit 0 on 3 shapes, real finding hidden); v0.4.17 refuses all 4; controls unchanged.
- Ladder `test/conform-unresolvable-accounts.test.mjs`: 6 red on pre-fix tree -> 10 green here; measurement pin (7); mutation ladder 6/6.
- Suite 796 -> 813 (809 pass / 4 named network skips / 0 fail).

### Limits

This is NOT an audit and there is no external user yet (0 stars, no third-party issues); the release is user-zero measured only, on one machine and one account, from committed fixtures — no live RPC shape was sampled for this pulse. The refusal is about a shape no reader can interpret — it does not decide what the right account is. The check covers indices at the `transactionInstructions` seam; a transaction that resolves every index still passes through `checkAccountList` unchanged. Older tags keep the defect (tags are immutable).

## Install

```bash
npm install github:auroraxo/sememe#v0.4.16
```

## The defect this release refuses (measured, not asserted)

`sememe conform <tx> --store <dir>` resolves each instruction's program from `instruction.programId` or by `programIdIndex` into the canonical key list. An index past the end of the list resolves to nothing — and the row loop **stepped over it**:

```js
for (const instruction of instructions) {
  if (!instruction.programId) continue;   // no row, no count, no refusal
```

The instruction vanished from `rows`, from `summary.instructions`, and from every verdict count. The report covered a **subset of the transaction it was handed** while describing itself as a check of that transaction.

Worst face, on the committed order-engine fixture (the fill instruction is the ONE instruction with a real disagreement — an undeclared signing account):

| case | v0.4.15 (published) | v0.4.16 |
|---|---|---|
| intact transaction | rows 12, `undeclared-signing-account: 1`, exit 1 | unchanged |
| fill index pushed past `accountKeys` | rows 11, `{no-stored-interface: 11}`, **exit 0** — the disagreement is HIDDEN | exit 1, `instruction-program-id-unresolvable` |
| extra appended instruction with a bad index | exit 0, rows 12 of 13 | exit 1, same reason |
| CPI (inner) instruction with a bad index | exit 0, rows 11 of 12 | exit 1, same reason |

## What changed

One refusal, `instruction-program-id-unresolvable`, raised **before** the store is read and **before** the filter selection. It names each offending instruction by position (top-level or `CPI of top-level #n`) and by the raw `programIdIndex` value it carried, plus the repair. The **all**-unresolvable case keeps its existing reason (`transaction-has-no-resolvable-program-id`) — pinned as a guard so the refusal does not drift. A filter that selects nothing still fires its own reason for callers whose argument is the problem.

## Evidence

- `research/conform-unresolvable-2026-11-11.json` — the SAME probe run in the pre-fix tree (`git archive 94aa00b`) and this tree: pre-fix exits 0 over the dropped instruction and the report **hides** the real finding; this tree refuses all three defect cases with the named reason; the intact control still exits 1 with its disagreement and the all-dropped control keeps its reason in **both** trees.
- Ladder `test/conform-unresolvable-program-id.test.mjs`: 6 red on the pre-fix tree → 16 green here (6 defect cases, 4 guards green on both trees).
- `test/conform-unresolvable-measurement.test.mjs` fails if the committed artifact stops being what the tool derives.
- Delivery measured on PUBLISHED TAGS (`tools/measure-conform-unresolvable-tag.mjs`, `research/conform-unresolvable-tag-2026-11-11.json`): v0.4.15 `carries-the-defect` — a subset report on all three dropped shapes, exit 0 with the real disagreement hidden on the worst face; v0.4.16 `refuses` — all three named refusals, no subset report, both controls unchanged.
- Tag pin `test/conform-unresolvable-tag-measurement.test.mjs`: 5 checks, including a falsification that the two tags' roles are not interchangeable.
- `tools/mutation-ladder-conform-unresolvable.sh`: 6/6 mutations caught (the refusal itself, the reason name, the refusal order vs the filter, the detail naming positions, the all-dropped reason staying put, CPI coverage).
- Full suite: 791 tests, 787 pass, 0 fail, 4 named network skips.

## Limits

One committed transaction fixture — no live RPC shape was sampled for this pulse. The refusal does not decide which program id is *right*, only that the gate must not guess about a shape it cannot read. Lookup-table addresses are still resolved through `meta.loadedAddresses` first (unchanged). No external users yet (user zero only), 0 stars, no audit — an own-host measurement on one machine with one account, not a statement that any third-party transaction shape behaves the same. v0.4.15 and older keep the defect (tags are immutable). npm registry publish is still credentials-blocked; the git tag is the release artifact.

## Install

```bash
npm install github:auroraxo/sememe#v0.4.15
```

## The defect this release refuses (measured, not asserted)

`sememe conform <tx> --store <dir>` is a CI gate: exit 1 on any disagreement, exit 0 when the checked instructions agree. It read the store through **one line that swallowed every failure** — `} catch { idl = null; }` — while `findStoredIdls` is the one store reader that refuses damage *by name* (a receipt whose object no longer re-hashes to its fingerprint, a receipt bound to another program, a missing object, a malformed receipt, a rewritten origin). `sememe decode` on such a store exits 1 with the reader's message; `sememe conform` on the **same store** turned that refusal into a verdict and exited 0.

Three faces of one defect, on the committed order-engine fixture:

| case | v0.4.14 (published) | v0.4.15 |
|---|---|---|
| tampered receipt fingerprint | exit 0, all `no-stored-interface` | exit 1, `store-reader-refused` |
| `--store` directory does not exist | exit 0 | exit 1, `no-sememe-store` |
| `objects/` but no `receipts/` | exit 0 | exit 1, `no-sememe-store` |

The tampered-receipt face is worse than a false green: the transaction's real disagreement (`undeclared-signing-account`) **disappeared** behind 12 green rows. Damage was indistinguishable from an acquisition gap — so the honest gap verdict was carrying a lie.

## What changed

The reader's two *absence* errors now carry machine-readable codes (`no-sememe-store`, `no-stored-idl`) with byte-identical messages. `checkTransaction` distinguishes exactly three cases: no receipt for this program → honest `no-stored-interface` row (the acquisition gap the coverage numbers depend on, unchanged); missing store → refused `no-sememe-store`; any other reader refusal → refused `store-reader-refused`. Both refusals exit 1, lead with the program id, and carry the reader's message plus the repair. The gate fails **closed** on stores it cannot read — a refusal is not a statement that the transaction disagrees.

## Evidence

- `research/conform-store-damage-2026-11-10.json` — same probe in the pre-fix tree and this tree: 3/3 faces green over an unreadable store before → 0/3 after, controls byte-identical, `hiddenDisagreement` measured.
- Ladder `test/conform-store-damage.test.mjs`: 7 red on the pre-fix tree → 11 green here; measurement test pins the committed artifact.
- `tools/mutation-ladder-conform-store-damage.sh`: 5/5 mutations caught.
- Full suite: 770 tests, 766 pass, 0 fail, 4 named network skips.

## Limits

No external users yet (user zero only), 0 stars, no audit — this is an own-host measurement on one machine with one account, not an audit and not a statement that any third-party store behaves the same. A refusal means the gate could not answer — it decides nothing about the transaction in that case. `--only` filtering still applies before the store is read. A program the store genuinely does not hold still produces `no-stored-interface`. Older tags keep their defects (tags are immutable). No npm registry publish; the git tag is the release artifact.

```js

```

The registry name is deliberately unpublished (no name squatting): the git tag is the release artifact.

## What's in v0.4.14

**A lock that pins nothing must not certify a store.**

`sememe lock` + `sememe verify --mode error` is the CI gate this project runs after checkout. Measured on the published `v0.4.13` install, two faces of one defect made that gate able to pass without checking anything:

```bash
npx sememe lock --store ./store --out ./sememe.lock   # store: receipts/ exists, no receipt in it
# -> { "lockVersion": 1, "programs": {} }, exit 0

npx sememe verify --store ./store --lock ./empty.lock --mode error
# -> { "pinned": 0, "violations": 0, "extra": [ ...18 real programs... ] }, exit 0
```

The first command wrote a lock pinning **zero** answers — no fingerprint, no receipt, no origin: nothing a drifted store could ever contradict. The second then certified a **real 18-program store** as clean against it. Every program appeared as an `extra`, and extras are never violations for being there (that rule is correct and stayed), so the report even *looked* informative while pinning nothing. `--mode warn` did the same.

Two refusals now happen, both named `lock-pins-nothing`:

- `sememe lock` over a store with no receipt **refuses and writes no file** — the refusal names the repair (`sememe pull` first). A store whose `receipts/` directory does not exist is still refused as `no sememe store`: the two refusals have different repairs.
- `sememe verify` against a lock whose `programs` map is empty **refuses in both modes** — the defect is a property of the *document*, not of the store, so `--mode warn` does not certify it either. The check runs after the `lockVersion` check, so an unsupported version is still reported as a version problem.

The ordinary journey is untouched: locking a real store writes a lock pinning every program, and verifying it against an intact store still exits 0.

**Measured** (`research/lock-nothing-pinned-2026-11-09.json`, the same probe file run in the pre-fix tree `git archive f22dbf5` and in this one): 3 defect faces green-over-nothing before, 0 after; the ordinary lock-then-verify journey exits 0 with 18 programs pinned in **both** trees. The published-tag side is measured separately (`research/lock-nothing-pinned-tag-2026-11-09.json`): v0.4.13 carries the defect on all three faces. Ladder `test/lock-nothing-pinned.test.mjs`: 5 red on the pre-fix tree, 12 green here, 6 guards green on both; 5/5 mutations caught by `tools/mutation-ladder-lock-nothing-pinned.sh`.

## Limits

- **No external users and no audit**: this release is verified only on the maintainer's own host, from fixtures. Zero stars, zero forks, zero outsiders so far.
- Fixture bytes, not a live RPC pull: the measurement runs from committed fixtures.
- `v0.4.13` and older keep the old behaviour — tags are immutable, and v0.4.13 carries this defect.
- npm registry publish is still blocked (no credentials); the git tag is the only install channel.

## What's in v0.4.13

**A CI gate that never ran must not exit 0.**

`sememe conform` is a gate: exit 1 on any disagreement, exit 0 when the checked instructions conform. `--only <program-id>` narrows the check to one program. Measured on the published `v0.4.12` install, a filter that selected **zero** instructions still exited **0**:

```bash
npx sememe conform <tx.json> --store ./store --only 6EF8rrecthR5Dkzon8Nwu78hRvfCKubJ14M5uBEwF6P
# -> { "rows": [], "summary": { "instructions": 0, ... } }, exit 0
```

The program id above is real — it just is not invoked by that transaction. A caller who mistyped the id they meant to gate on was told the transaction conformed. The second face of the same defect: `--only not-a-program-id` produced the identical empty green, and the value was never validated as a program id at all.

Two refusals now happen **before the store is read**:

- `filter-is-not-a-program-id` — the value is not a canonical 32-byte base58 program id; it can never match an instruction.
- `filter-matched-no-instruction` — the filter selects none of this transaction's instructions, and the refusal **names the programs the transaction actually invokes**, so a typo is visible instead of green.

The unfiltered check and a filter that does match are untouched.

**Measured** (`research/conform-filter-domain-2026-11-09.json`, same probe run in the pre-fix tree and in this one): 2 defect cases green-over-0-instructions before, 0 after; guards unchanged. 16 tests on the fix, 6 red on the pre-fix tree, 5/5 mutations caught.

- The filter refusal covers `conform --only`; it does not make a conform report meaningful for a program with no stored interface.

## What's in v0.4.12

**Account union — two verified sources, one account, byte evidence decides.**

Union decode has covered instructions and events since v0.4.0. Accounts never got the second half: `sememe account` read exactly ONE receipt, so a store holding two verified copies of a program had two opinions about an account's layout and only one of them was ever consulted. This release closes that half.

```bash
npx sememe account --union 6EF8rrecthR5Dkzon8Nwu78hRvfCKubJ14M5uBEwF6P <base64> --store ./store
```

**Measured on 12 real mainnet pump.fun accounts** (`research/account-union-2026-11-08.json`; the two committed copies genuinely disagree about `BondingCurve` — 13 fields on chain, 19 in the published copy):

| | single receipt (before) | `account --union` |
|---|---|---|
| byte-exact | **0 / 12** | **6 / 12** |
| bytes left unexplained | **12 / 12** | 6 / 12 |
| verdict | one source, no verdict | `layout_drift` 6, `agree` 6 |

The 6 recovered accounts are the ones where the published copy reproduces every byte and the on-chain copy leaves 41 (and 1) unexplained — byte evidence picks the published copy and records why. The 6 `UserVolumeAccumulator` accounts read `agree`: both copies say the same thing and **both** leave 31 bytes unexplained. Agreement is reported, never papered over as coverage.

**The rules, because an arbitration is only as good as its refusals:**

- **A fallback needs byte evidence.** A source that names an account it cannot reproduce is refused. The honest no-evidence state is reachable and is pinned with a real codec property rather than a mock: an `f32` field holding a *signalling* NaN decodes to `null` and re-encodes to a different bit pattern — the decode succeeds, consumes the whole account, and reproduces nothing.
- **When the evidence ties, the primary stands.** Two layouts can serialise to the same bytes and decode to different values (`u32` vs `i32` over `0xffffffff`): both are `full_roundtrip`, so the on-chain pull answers and the drift is reported — never resolved by preference.
- **Two different account names for the same 8 bytes is a hard refusal**, not a decision to make.
- **The plain path is untouched.** `sememe account` still reads one receipt and carries no `view`; the union is a flag, not a behaviour change.

**The harvester no longer dies on a public endpoint's batch cap.** `tools/account-harvest.mjs` died on its first oversized `getMultipleAccounts` batch (one public endpoint caps it at 10) — no fixture written, and a refusal that did not name the cap as the whole story. The cap is now read from the server's own sentence and the batch shrinks **without skipping keys** (a shrink that skipped would silently under-sample and report fewer accounts as if that were all there were); the fixture records the batch size it actually got.

14 new tests pin the behaviour, each asserting a VERDICT rather than just a decode, and two mutations were verified red on either side of their fix before landing.

## Honest limits

No external users yet (0 non-owner signals), not an audit, own-host measurement. A byte-exact round trip proves the bytes are *reproduced*, not that the field names mean what the program intends. The published copy is adopted content whose origin stays **declared**, never verified against the deployed program — that item remains open. One program, one account window: this measures a drift that exists, not how common it is across the ecosystem. `v0.4.11` and earlier keep their behaviour (tags are immutable); their limits are named on their own pages.

## What's in v0.4.11

Five measured fixes, all of them found by running the product against a store it should have handled — not by reading the code.

- **A crashed write must not brick the store.** sememe installs every receipt through a temporary file `<name>.tmp-<pid>-<random>` in the SAME `receipts/` directory and removes it in a `finally`; a crash between the write and the cleanup (SIGKILL, OOM, power loss) leaves that file behind forever — and every reader treated EVERY file in `receipts/` as a receipt. Measured on the published `v0.4.10` install, one leftover `.tmp-4711-9f2c1a` file broke every surface at once: `sememe decode` exited 1 ("store receipt … is unreadable"), `sememe decode --union` exited 1, `sememe lock` exited 1 ("Cannot destructure property 'idl'"), and `sememe verify --mode error` went **red over a perfectly intact program** while naming no repair. One classifier (`src/receipt-name.mjs`) now separates four kinds: a well-formed `receipt` (read as before), a `malformed` receipt-shaped name (DAMAGE — still refused by name, because ignoring it would be a new green lie), sememe's own `debris` (safe to ignore: the install hard-links the temporary to its final name, so the temp never holds information the committed receipt does not), and `foreign` (never a program). Debris and foreign files are ignored but never silently — `verify`'s report gains a `stray` field naming each file and its kind.
- **A CI gate must not be green over a store the reader refuses.** `writeLock` re-checked every receipt, `checkLock` only the pinned ones: `sememe lock` exited 1 while `sememe verify` exited 0 with violations 0 — a green CI gate over a program whose decode exits 1. Extras now run through the same helper; damage in an unpinned program is a violation marked `scope: "extra"`, so pin drift is not misread as the cause.
- **A lock that pins no origin must not certify a declared origin.** A legacy lock (written before origin pinning) left the comparison unrun, so a rewritten `receipt.origin` passed the gate as verified. The store now reports `unbound` — exit 1, repair named.
- **A declared origin is declared, not verified.** Origins are qualified as `declared` on every reader surface and bound to the receipt by digest; rewriting one is reported as `relabelled`.
- **The test harness no longer races itself.** Six test files packed into the shared repo root and renamed each other's tarball away (ENOENT under a parallel suite); each now packs into its own directory.

The measurement ships as an instrument, not a claim: `tools/measure-receipt-hygiene.mjs` derives both committed artifacts — `research/receipt-hygiene-2026-11-07-before.json` (the published v0.4.10 install: 6 contract violations) and `research/receipt-hygiene-2026-11-07.json` (this tag: 0) — and `test/receipt-hygiene-measurement.test.mjs` fails if a committed report stops being what the tool derives. Seventeen new tests pin the behaviour (three green guards that must stay green on the pre-fix tree, six that were red there, four mutations that must each turn a test red, four pinning the artifacts).

## Honest limits

No external users yet (0 non-owner signals), not an audit, own-host measurement. The before/after artifacts were both measured on this host; the tag journeys measure the exact bytes an install receives, but it is still one machine and my own account. The classifier was checked against 256 real receipt names (0 unmatched), but no store outside this host has been observed. An adopted receipt's `origin` remains a declared label, not a verified origin — honest labelling of provenance is still open. `v0.4.10` and earlier keep their behaviour (tags are immutable); their defects are named on this page, and the v0.4.10 release page carries a SUPERSEDED banner pointing here.

## What's in v0.4.10

- **One store answers with ONE receipt, whichever command reads it.** Measured on the published v0.4.9 install (`github:auroraxo/sememe#v0.4.9` in an empty app, no clone) with a store whose two ON-CHAIN receipts of one program carry slot strings of different digit length: `sememe decode` read the OLDER slot `99999999` and refused `sell_v3` (`unknown instruction discriminator 1c92de7726c469d5`, exit 1), while `sememe decode --union` read the newer slot `123456789` and decoded it, and `sememe lock` pinned `99999999` — a third surface, a second receipt. Two sorts, two winners: the union path has always sorted on-chain receipts by NUMERIC slot, while the plain reader and `src/lock.mjs` sorted by receipt FILENAME — and a decimal string sorts by its digits, not by its value. One comparator (`src/receipt-order.mjs`) now rules the plain reader, the union path and both lock paths: slot numerically first, filename byte-wise as tiebreak.
- **The measurement ships as an instrument, not a claim.** `tools/measure-slot-order.mjs` derives both committed artifacts — `research/slot-order-2026-11-07-before.json` (the published v0.4.9 install: 5 contract violations) and `research/slot-order-2026-11-07.json` (this tree: 0) — and `test/slot-order-measurement.test.mjs` fails if a committed report stops being what the tool derives. Nine new store tests pin the ordering (three of them RED on the pre-fix tree, plus two mutations that must each turn a test red), and the multi-copy ladder gains O6: a SECOND program with only adopted copies — plain, union and lock name the same receipt, and a damaged second copy refuses the lock and is named at verify time.
- **Reachability stated honestly.** All 44,661 live slot values across `research/` and fixtures are 9 digits (`462039125..465713413`), so two receipts written by `pull` today have equal-length slots and both orderings agree — the defect is LATENT for a fresh pull and becomes LIVE for stores whose slot strings differ in length (another era or cluster, a hand-assembled store, or mainnet crossing 1,000,000,000). The equal-length control case is green on both sides of the fix: this release changes the defective case only.

Eighth release-page note of the class this repo keeps measuring — main fixed, the pin pointing at a tag behind it: v0.4.1, v0.4.3, v0.4.4, v0.4.5, v0.4.6, v0.4.7, v0.4.8 (two verdicts from one store), now v0.4.9 (one store, two receipts, a lock pinning a third surface's pick). The instrument that measures the PUBLISHED tag itself now covers this too: the journey test installs exactly what the README pins.

## What's in v0.4.5

- **A base58 payload is a payload.** The CLI has always documented "base58 or hex" for every payload argument, but the base58 path decoded to a byte array that was not a `Buffer`, and three consumers need `Buffer` methods. So the SAME bytes behaved differently depending on how they were written — measured against the PUBLISHED v0.4.4 install (a pinned install of tag `v0.4.4`), not against a working tree:
  - `sememe decode --union <program> <base58>` failed on EVERY base58 payload with `unionDecode needs the payload bytes as a Buffer`, while the same payload as hex decoded fine. The README's own union walkthrough uses a base58 payload, so it could not run.
  - an `f64`/`f32` argument died with `slice.readDoubleLE is not a function` (measured on OpenBook v2 `stubOracleCreate`, price 1.5).
  - a `bytes` argument came out as a comma-separated byte list (`1,2,3,255`) instead of base64 (`AQID/w==`) — silent corruption, not an error.
- **The fix is in three layers.** Root cause: `decodeBase58` returns a `Buffer` (a `Buffer` IS a `Uint8Array`, so every existing caller keeps working). The codec's `Cursor` normalizes its bytes to a `Buffer` once, so the shape of the input cannot decide whether it decodes. The union path normalizes instead of refusing, and still refuses input that is not a byte array at all.
- **`test/base58-payload-bytes.test.mjs` pins the equality.** For each of the three cases, the base58 form and the hex form must produce the same instruction, the same fields and the same verdict — plus the CLI end to end. Two mutations (revert `decodeBase58`; remove the `Cursor` guard) must turn the contract red, so the guards are not decorative. Suite: 515 tests, 513 pass, 2 named-skip, 0 fail.
